name: Access Control Bypass
description: Ability to assess and bypass electronic and physical access control systems as part of authorised security assessments. Covers RFID/NFC badge cloning, access control system architecture assessment, tailgating, door hardware bypass (request-to-exit sensors, door gap tools), and evaluation of access control policies and configurations.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to access control systems or bypass techniques

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands common access control technologies and their general weaknesses
evidence: Completed access control systems fundamentals training
Can identify common access control technologies (proximity cards, smart cards, biometrics, keypads)
Understands the difference between low-frequency (125kHz) and high-frequency (13.56MHz) card systems

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Performs basic access control assessments and bypass under supervision
evidence: Cloned low-frequency proximity cards in lab environment using Proxmark or similar
Performed tailgating exercises under supervision during physical assessments
Used basic door bypass tools (under-door tools, shims) in lab training
Carried signed authorisation and engagement contact details on every on-site exercise, and followed the agreed procedure when challenged

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses and bypasses standard access control systems on engagements
evidence: Conducted access control assessments on 3+ physical penetration tests
Successfully cloned access badges and used them to gain entry on live engagements
Identified and exploited request-to-exit sensor weaknesses and door hardware gaps
Documented access control weaknesses with evidence for client reports

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Bypasses advanced access control systems; assesses system architecture; mentors team
evidence: Assessed high-frequency smart card deployments (e.g., legacy iCLASS, MIFARE Classic, DESFire) for weaknesses such as UID-only reads, default or diversified-key flaws, and downgrade, and bypassed multi-factor access control where weaknesses allowed
Evaluated access control system architecture and policy configurations
Developed access control bypass toolkits and methodologies for the lab
Mentors team on access control technology and bypass techniques

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Researches access control vulnerabilities; defines lab methodology; recognised specialist
evidence: Discovered or published vulnerabilities in commercial access control systems
Authored the lab's access control assessment methodology
Trains teams on access control technology, from card systems to biometrics
Recognised as the lab's authority on electronic access control security

assessment_methods.description: Given a lab-configured access control system, identify the technology, assess weaknesses, and demonstrate bypass within a time constraint
Review access control assessment findings from recent physical penetration test reports

equipment: Under-door tool and door bypass toolkit
